svg.text: A visual introduction to information theory — recorded as a DL knowledge base
Pinkard & Waller, arXiv:2206.07867v3, reflected into Lean 4 as DL.IT.itKB (proved consistent by an explicit model).
Colours = semantic families · emoji = icons · DL notation = symbols · glosses = words — rows are generated from the reflected base and universal TBox/ABox data.
arrow C → D reads "C ⊑ D" (every C is a D); dashed = disjoint
B. Terminological axioms (TBox) — the paper's definitional relationships
Every random variable has a probability distribution over its outcomes.
Every random variable has outcomes drawn from a discrete outcome space.
Every random variable has an entropy measuring its average uncertainty.
A stochastic process is an ordered sequence of random variables.
A source of random events is a random variable.
The channel capacity is the maximal mutual information, hence a mutual information.
A typical sequence is an outcome (of a length-N sequence of events).
The messages of a source are its outcomes.
A noiseless channel is a channel (its conditional distribution is deterministic).
A noisy channel is a channel.
Noiseless and noisy channels are disjoint: a channel is one or the other.
A channel maps inputs (a random variable) to outputs.
A channel produces outputs (a random variable) from its inputs.
A prefix code is a code in which no codeword is a prefix of another.
An encoder maps messages to channel inputs (a random variable).
C. Assertional axioms (ABox) — the running colored-marble (§2.1–2.2) and colour/shape (§2.5) examples
The urn draw is a random variable X.
X has the marble colour distribution.
Blue is an outcome of X.
The marble source's entropy is that of X.
Colour X is a random variable.
Shape Y is a random variable.
The marble colours follow a probability distribution.
The marble source has an entropy (e.g. 1.75 or 2 bits).
Colour and shape share a mutual information I(X;Y).
D. Legend — colour families & the many-minds reading guide
E. Information prism — moonshine or shadow
Some information carries the Monster ↔ modular-form correspondence and becomes moonshine.
Every non-moonshine information item becomes shadow: Information ⊓ ¬MoonshineInformation ⊑ ShadowInformation.
‘Shadow’ here is the classifier complement, not the analytic shadow of a mock modular form.
F. Universal ontology — everything discussed, inside one reflected TBox/ABox
Thing ≡ ⊤ includes every object semantically; the finite ABox below inventories every major project stratum without claiming to enumerate mathematics.
Every domain object is a Thing.
Every project artifact is a thing.
Every formal artifact is a project artifact.
Every Lean module is a formal artifact.
A proof certificate is a formal artifact.
Every generated visualization is a project artifact.
Every represented software object is a thing.
A knowledge base is both a Lean module and an ontology entity.
Every meta-ontology entity is itself an ontology entity.
Every represented mathematical object is a thing.
Represented mathematical-physics objects are mathematical objects.
The source paper is a document.
Universal ABox — all 30 inventory assertions and links
The complete Lean project is a software object.
The uploaded information-theory paper is the source document.
The Description Logic core is a Lean module.
The paper's base TBox/ABox is a knowledge base.
The full-paper extension is a knowledge base.
The cross-domain merged ontology is a knowledge base.
The derived cross-domain weave is an ontology entity.
The carried-higher-level ontology is a meta-ontology entity.
This scope-complete ontology is itself represented at the meta level.
Entropy and mutual-information results are information-theory objects.
Coding and Reed–Solomon results are information-theory objects.
The reflection and reconstruction machinery is a Lean module.
Monster, umbral, and modular-form material is represented as moonshine mathematics.
Lagrangian and CFT material is represented as mathematical physics.
PDE, Maass-form, and spectral-complexity material is represented as mathematical physics.
A model-checking theorem certifies this ontology's consistency.
README and supporting reports document the project.
The bounded FNORD lexicon is included as a formal module.
Self-description, self-import, and self-image are included as formal modules.
The universal ontology is part of the project.
The universal ontology describes the base ontology.
The universal ontology describes the merged ontology.
The universal ontology describes the prior meta ontology.
The universal ontology records itself without leaving the logic.
The certificate verifies the reflected universal ontology.
The base graphic visualizes the base ontology.
The meta graphic visualizes the meta ontology.
The documentation is about the complete project.
Generated by RequestProject/Visualize.lean from DL.IT.itKB and DL.Universal.universalKB. Both have explicit consistency models; annotations reflect into Lean semantics.
